PullRequest.Title: Ensure test diagnostic artifact directories exist
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #272563.

## Why

In [build 366411](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=366411), attempt 1 failed first in WebKit unit tests. Integration/smoke tests were then skipped, and the subsequent 1ES checks and artifact publication failed again because `.build/logs` and `.build/crashes` did not exist. The successful second attempt did not fix this failure path.

## Changes

- Add one shared, inline PowerShell template for the two optional diagnostic directories. Use explicit source-directory paths and the agent build directory as the working directory so initialization does not depend on successful checkout or dependency installation.
- Opt in test-enabled macOS, Linux, and Windows jobs after checkout and the credential-sensitive LFS cache fetch, but before tool/dependency setup. Jobs without tests remain unchanged.
- Reuse the helper in the flaky build and unit/integration/smoke job templates. Preserve the flaky build's existing post-compile placement and `always()` condition.
- Use `System.IO.Directory.CreateDirectory` to preserve existing contents and fail explicitly on file/directory collisions. Local validation caught that `New-Item -Force` silently accepts those collisions.

Test exit codes, artifact publication conditions, and 1ES non-production validation remain unchanged. This addresses the secondary diagnostic-collection errors, not the unrelated historical WebKit test failures.

Scenarios.Scenario: Standard macOS, Linux, and Windows test-enabled compile jobs (Electron, Browser, or Remote suites)
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After checkout (and the Electron-only test-cache fetch), the new PowerShell task must finish before NodeTool, dependency setup, compilation, and tests. The work is on the job critical path but consists of one process invocation and two directory checks/creates.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch a pwsh task to initialize diagnostic directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one PowerShell process per test-enabled job attempt, not per test or artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These compile templates had no early diagnostic-directory subprocess; directories could be created later by tests, leaving early failures without valid artifact paths.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The task completes before all tool setup and build/test work, adding a constant serial step.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly two CreateDirectory calls per affected job attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No corresponding early filesystem operations occurred in these compile templates; some Electron test steps created .build/crashes later.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Two local filesystem metadata operations complete before the job proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish crash and log pipeline artifacts at job completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to two existing artifact publications per affected job; upload bytes scale only with diagnostics actually produced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The publication outputs already existed. Normal runs with generated directories already published them; on sufficiently early failures they could fail because the target path did not exist. The diff makes those existing outputs viable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Post-job artifact publication can extend completion, especially on failure, but it is not moved earlier and does not block compilation or tests.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One invocation per test-enabled job, independent of test count. Current CI expansion creates three suite jobs per platform, so up to nine jobs perform it in parallel; retries add one invocation per job attempt.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The task is serial within each job. Separate platform/suite jobs run with pipeline-level parallelism; there is no inner concurrency or per-test fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no application cache. On a clean checkout the directories are absent and are created; if retained by the agent, CreateDirectory performs idempotent metadata checks. Checkout cleaning can remove untracked directories before this step.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in one new serial subprocess and two filesystem calls per affected job; pipeline callers explicitly set one of the three test-suite flags.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent task startup duration varies, but work remains constant per job and negligible relative to dependency installation, compilation, and test durations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded constant startup work to guarantee diagnostics on early failures; it does not scale with tests, repository size, or artifact count and introduces no burst within a job.

Scenarios.Scenario: Shared flaky build jobs on macOS, Linux, and Windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The diagnostic initialization runs after the full compile template and before smoke/integration compilation and workspace archiving. Its always() condition also executes it after compile failure, before existing diagnostic publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the shared PowerShell directory initializer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One process per platform build job attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The template already launched one powershell process on Windows or one shell/mkdir process on macOS/Linux at this exact point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Same post-compile serial placement as the replaced platform-specific task.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or verify the crash and log directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two directory operations per build job attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The replaced commands already created exactly the same two directories with mkdir -p or New-Item -Force.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Constant local metadata work before archive/test compilation continues.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish existing crash and log pipeline artifacts after the job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two existing outputs per build attempt; bytes depend on diagnostics produced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The outputs and directory initialization already existed; the PR changes implementation, not upload count on paths where initialization succeeded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Post-job publication only; ensuring paths prevents secondary publication errors after compile failure.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One shared build job per selected platform and one directory-initialization task per job attempt. Test iteration count does not multiply this step.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial within each shared build job; platform build jobs may run in parallel. Two directory calls execute sequentially in one PowerShell process.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. The compile checkout cleans untracked files; CreateDirectory preserves existing diagnostics generated during compile and otherwise creates empty paths.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that cardinality and placement are unchanged because the shared template directly replaces one platform-selected task.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: PowerShell versus shell startup can differ on Unix agents, but it remains a single constant task in a long compile job and no evidence establishes a meaningful latency regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The refactor preserves one task and two filesystem operations; any Unix process-startup delta is a speculative micro-cost without realistic scaling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Flaky unit, integration, and smoke test jobs with repeated test iterations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The initializer runs immediately after checkout:none and before artifact downloads, extraction, tool setup, and every test iteration. It ensures post-job diagnostic outputs have valid paths even if setup fails.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One process per flaky test job attempt, independent of iteration count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every flaky test job already launched one platform-specific powershell or shell task at this point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before artifact download and all tests, matching the replaced step's placement.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The replaced task already created both paths once per job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Constant local filesystem setup before downloads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download build artifacts before tests and publish crash/log artifacts afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Downloads equal the configured grouped artifacts (one for unit, two for smoke, three for integration); two diagnostic outputs are published. Neither count depends on test iterations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same downloads and publications occurred after the old directory-creation task.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Downloads are on setup critical path and publication is post-job, but neither boundary was introduced or moved by this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One initialization per selected test job, up to unit/integration/smoke across each of three platforms (nine jobs). The iterations collection can be large, but initialization remains once per job rather than once per iteration.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial within each test job. Selected test jobs depend on their platform's shared build, then may run in parallel; no shared limiter is relevant because each performs only two local metadata operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache. Jobs begin without checkout and generally reconstruct Build.SourcesDirectory from downloaded archives; the initializer creates the directory tree once and extraction reuses it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from all nine template call sites that initialization occurs once at job scope, outside iteration loops.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact cross-platform startup difference between pwsh and the prior Unix shell is unmeasured; effective operation count is unchanged and test iterations do not amplify it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The helper preserves the existing job-level work and avoids per-iteration or per-artifact fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Early-failure diagnostic collection and artifact publication
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When checkout, setup, compilation, or tests fail, the initializer either has already run or, in the flaky build, runs under always(). Existing pipeline artifact outputs then execute during job finalization. This is off the successful build/test critical path except for the small initialization step.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ensure artifact source paths exist without deleting existing contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two idempotent calls per relevant job attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Standard test compile jobs lacked this early guarantee; flaky jobs already had it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Allows failure finalization to proceed to existing artifact collection rather than encountering a missing path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: templateContext pipelineArtifact outputs in affected job templates
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Upload existing crash/log pipeline artifacts during finalization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two diagnostic uploads per job attempt; empty or populated according to failure timing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Outputs already attempted publication. On early failure with absent paths they could fail fast; after this diff they can publish empty or available diagnostics.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can add bounded failure-finalization time, intentionally preserving diagnostics; it does not delay a successful test's main execution path beyond the initializer itself.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two directories and at most two diagnostic artifact publications per job attempt. Upload cost scales with actual crash/log bytes, not repository size or number of tests directly.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Directory creation is sequential in one task. Artifact outputs are managed by the pipeline after job steps; the diff adds no explicit parallel publication or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No caching or coalescing is added. Empty directories yield minimal artifacts; populated directories retain the existing diagnostics and publication behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the network outputs pre-exist and that the changed task only enables their intended execution on early failures.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Failure artifact byte volume is workload-dependent, but the PR neither removes size bounds nor increases generated diagnostics; it only guarantees source paths.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Any added failure-finalization work is the bounded, intentional diagnostic publication already configured by the pipeline, not a newly scaling performance mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and their pipeline callers. The only new normal-path work is one PowerShell task with two idempotent local directory operations per test-enabled job; flaky jobs replace equivalent existing setup. No high-confidence, actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
